title: Compatible coefficient maps give a linear strict tensor tower
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small relative to the module universe and let $R,S,B_n$ ($n\geq1$) be sheaves of commutative rings. Let $r_n:R\to B_n$, $p_n:S\to B_n$ and $b_n:B_{n+1}\to B_n$ satisfy $b_nr_{n+1}=r_n$ and $b_np_{n+1}=p_n$. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], strict towers [def-weil-inverse-system] and cochain complexes [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For an $R$-module $M$ set $V_n(M)=\operatorname{Res}_{p_n}(M\otimes_R B_n)$, with transition $x\otimes z\mapsto x\otimes b_n(z)$. These maps exist uniquely with the displayed formula on the images of presheaf pure tensors and define an additive functor $V:\operatorname{Mod}(R)\to\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Mod}(S))$ sending $f$ to $(f\otimes1)_n$. On complexes the transitions commute with the termwise integer-shift comparisons. Its termwise cochain functor preserves homotopies and has coherent integer-shift comparisons. Restriction along each $p_n$ preserves and reflects quasi-isomorphisms. If $k$ is a commutative ring with compatible homomorphisms to the rings of global sections of $R,S$ whose composites into every $B_n$ agree, the induced scalar actions make $V$ $k$-linear [def-weil-linear-category, def-weil-linear-functor].
